 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.46/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Taliparamba,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 28/05/2019.
The respondents herein are respondents 1 to 3 respectively in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 02/05/2016 at about 05:00 p.m., while she was standing in a bus stop situated in front of Snake Park, Parassinikadavu, scooter bearing registration no.KL-13-S-1712 ridden by the second respondent in a rash and 2025:KER:72749 MACA NO. 417 OF 2020 negligent manner knocked her down, as a result of which she sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 4,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner of the offending vehicle filed written statement contending that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the claim petitioner.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.

4. The second respondent/rider of the offending vehicle remained ex parte.
5.
The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle, but denied liability.
It was contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.

Padmakshi K.K vs Mahroof K.P on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189420326/
2 6.
Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A7 series and Ext.X1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner and Exts.B1 to B3 were marked on the side of the respondents.

The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent/rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,09,800/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realization along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
8. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
9. Heard both sides 10.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a daily labourer, was earning 450/- per day.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 7,000/- per 2025:KER:72749 MACA NO. 417 OF 2020 month, which is quite low going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011)
13 SCC 236.
10.1.

sentences.text: In the light of the dictum in the Ramachandrappa (Supra), I find that the notional income of the claim petitioner can be fixed at 10,500/- per month.
Loss of earnings 11.
The materials on record show that the claim petitioner had sustained left temporal contusion with left fronto-temporal SDH.
She was hospitalized for a period of 10 days.
In all probability, she might have been unable to work for a period of 6 months.
Therefore, I find that she can be granted compensation towards loss of earnings for a period of 6 months, which comes to 63,000/- (10,500 x 6 months).
Transportation charges 12.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the amount awarded under this head, that is, 2025:KER:72749 MACA NO. 417 OF 2020 1,200/-, is quite low.
The Tribunal has not awarded compensation for the expenses incurred for taking the claim petitioner from the hospital to her residence and hence interference on the said aspect is required.
12.1. On going through the claim petition, I find absolutely no pleadings regarding the transportation expenses alleged to have been incurred by the claim petitioner.

When this aspect was Padmakshi K.K vs Mahroof K.P on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189420326/
3 pointed out, the learned counsel for the claim petitioner draws my attention to ground no.(I) in the appeal memorandum which reads thus:-
"I.
It is submitted that the immediately after the accident the appellant was taken to Lourde hospital, Taliparamba and thereafter Pariyaram Medical College Hospital.
The injuries were in a critical condition.
The Tribunal awarded only meager amount as a compensation for transport to hospital.
The court below ought to have awarded more amounts to the appellant towards compensation for transport to hospital considering the distance from the place of accident to hospital."
(Emphasis supplied) 2025:KER:72749 MACA NO. 417 OF 2020
As is evident, in the appeal memorandum also, there is no ground that compensation has not been awarded for the expenses incurred for taking the claim petitioner from the hospital to her house.
When this aspect was pointed out, the learned counsel for the claim petitioner submitted that it is just and fair compensation that needs to be awarded and hence reasonable amount may be granted.
This submission is opposed by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer, who submits that the amount that has already been granted is reasonable and so no enhancement is called for.
12.2. The distance from Lourde Hospital, Taliparamba to Pariyaram Medical College Hospital referred to in the appeal memorandum is stated to be 12 kilometers.
The Tribunal has granted an amount of 1,200/- which seems to be reasonable.

As noticed earlier, there is no ground(s) raised either in the claim petition or in the appeal memorandum regarding the distance or the expenses incurred for taking the claim petitioner from the hospital to her residence.
During the course of arguments, it is submitted 2025:KER:72749 MACA NO. 417 OF 2020 that the distance from the hospital to the residence of the claim petitioner is 32 kilometers.
In the interest of justice and in the absence of any pleadings or evidence on this aspect, an amount of 1,000/- more is awarded under this head.
Pain & sufferings 13.
Though an amount of 1,00,000/- was claimed, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 30,000/-.
In the light of the injuries sustained and the period of hospitalization, I find that an amount of 55,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Compensation for loss of amenities and enjoyment of life 14.
Though no amount was claimed, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 10,000/- which is also stated to be on the lower side.
Taking into account the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that an amount of 25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

15. The impugned Award is modified to the following extent:

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 1,31,430/- (total 2025:KER:72749 MACA NO. 417 OF 2020 compensation = 4,41,230/- that is, 3,09,800/- granted by the Tribunal plus 1,31,430/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 102 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
The liberty granted to the third respondent/insurer to recover the amount from respondents 1 and 2 shall stand confirmed.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
